column1: # lock-closure-receipts.tsv — reviewed closure receipts for actions.lock.
# A row says: "at this exact commit, the named source uses this external ref,
# written in lock-key form." The rows for one `owner/repo@sha` are the UNION of
# external `uses:` across the files this repository calls at that commit, and
# the union of external `uses:` of an external composite action's action.yml.
# The audit compares each record's nested `uses:` list against the union; a
# short list is a dropped edge (CLOSURE-DROPPED), an extra row is an unreviewed
# Why a checked-in receipt exists at all: `gh actions-lock` writes a record's
# nested edges from the pinned source, and a later regeneration can shorten
# that list without creating any dangling ref. No ref is then unresolvable, so
# clauses 1-4 of scripts/check-lock-sync.sh all pass while the composite's or
# reusable's real dependency set is no longer represented. The receipt is the
# reviewed snapshot that makes the loss observable.
#     source: action.yml at the commit the tag v5.0.0 resolved to when the lock
#             record was written (fc324d3 is the reviewed immutable commit)
# Receipts are SHA-bound on purpose. When a tag moves, the record's commit does
# not move with it (that is the point of preserving the resolved commit), so a
# receipt stays valid for the reviewed snapshot. To re-review a snapshot, emit a
# new receipt for the new commit and remove the old rows in the same change.
